Lacy's *Gemini Rights* (released July 15, 2022) is largely built around his breakup, and his interviews describe the album as a way of working through it.

- **Framing:** In a GRAMMY.com interview, he described the record as him coming into himself after a breakup, and said he saw it as more hopeful than sad, centered on finding happiness.
- **Opening track "Static":** He told W magazine he wrote it two or three weeks after the split, and that the song is about refusing to escape the pain through a rebound. Per Songfacts, the relationship ended in November 2021 after seven months together.
- **Why it ended:** Speaking to The Guardian, he said nothing was working despite repeated attempts, and that the couple tried to reconcile but it didn't work out.
- **The ex's reaction:** Per Songfacts, Lacy said his ex liked it, though some lines prompted a reaction.
- **Creative process:** Lacy's artist statement on Apple Music says that once he understood that artists and audiences aren't separate, the album felt very easy and fun to make. He also said the biggest lesson from the process was about how small people make love, and that he wants to love unconditionally.
- **Other details:** The album was majorly self-produced by Lacy, with John Carroll Kirby co-writing "Static" (per Songfacts).

Sources were GRAMMY.com, W magazine (via Songfacts), The Guardian (via Songfacts), Apple Music, and AOL. The interviews are dated 2022 and the breakup details come from Lacy's own accounts, so they are his perspective rather than independently verified.

- **Owning his narrative:** Secondary coverage quotes the 2022 Guardian interview on Lacy's wish to control his own story and avoid being labeled, tied to his experience of homophobia as a kid (he told The Guardian about owning his narrative and not wanting to do things that would put a title on him).
- **Breakup comments:** Lacy reportedly told The Guardian that he kept trying to communicate with his ex during their seven-month relationship, but it wasn't working, and that he still loves him and made a great record (per the same coverage, he said he tried repeatedly and nothing worked, and that despite it all he still loved the ex).
- **Album context:** The album was inspired by a failed relationship that Lacy himself ended. Much of the album concerns the aftermath of a love affair with another man, but he still resists attaching any specific label to his sexuality.
- **Guardian on identity:** One outlet says Lacy told The Guardian he didn't feel as "flamboyant" as the men attracted to men he saw in the media (he talks about not feeling as "flamboyant" as the media's examples).
- **Reception:** Gemini Rights won the Grammy for Best Urban Contemporary album. "Bad Habit" charted at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.
- **Follow-up:** Lacy revealed that he's planning to release his next album, OH YEAH?, in the coming months. It's the follow-up to 2022's Gemini Rights.

Apollo XXI wasn't made on an iPhone. The iPhone work is Lacy's earlier material, and the sources describe Gemini Rights as the studio project.

- **Apollo XXI (2019):** One review says Lacy cooked up his first proper album, Apollo XXI, on his laptop. Crack Magazine similarly says he self-produced his debut Apollo XXI entirely on his laptop.
- **iPhone work:** The iPhone-made material is the earlier six-song Steve Lacy's Demo, alone on his iPhone, plus "Dark Red," which he literally made on his iPhone. Crack also credits him with producing Kendrick Lamar's "PRIDE" on his iPhone.
- **Gemini Rights (2022):** One review describes it as the delightfully cacophonous brainchild of co-writers and outside producers and musicians under Lacy's leadership in a proper studio. Crack says that for his second LP, though, Lacy has opted for the full studio treatment. A Northern Transmissions piece, however, says the album was written, produced, and played pretty much entirely by Lacy. So the sources agree on the studio approach but differ on how much outside help was involved.
